title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on P111 and type-(4,4) P104 units (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p111-p104-44/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

PR #1212 (burntout76) proves rank-8 gauge rigidity, K = D(2G)D⁻¹, of the masked (E-graph) system on P112, P120 and the type-(2,2,2,2) P104 units. Its PROOF.md §10 leaves two gaps, and this PR closes both:

- **P111 (all 112 units):** Lemma 5′ covers a class with three live rows. Case (ii) has rank 1 < 3, as #1212 noted. The new part is the `b` side: the three pairwise sign products span the non-trivial characters, so γγ′ is constant.
- **Type-(4,4) P104 (28 units):** Lemma 6′ is a gluing lemma. It needs only connectivity of the usable classes through each pivot pair, plus an explicit three-triple path. The argument is multiplicative, so it holds over any field of characteristic 0. It works with 12/14 usable blocks.

**Consequence.** In the E-graph model, decoders with exactly eight costly terms have cst ≥ 63 on every P111 unit (attained by PR717's P111 decoders) and cst ≥ 56 on every type-(4,4) unit. Sharpness of 56 on the type-(4,4) units is not checked.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p111-p104-44/verify.py` runs 26 exact checks and 4 controls in about 1 s. It is an independent implementation with its own E8 model, classes, witnesses, gluing and assembly, and imports nothing from #1212. The controls show:
  - two-row classes are not forced;
  - P111 needs Lemma 5′;
  - the path condition rejects a rank-17 block set;
  - a perturbed entry breaks (2).
- `--pr1212-dir <checkout of 57099cb5>` checks the git blobs of #1212's `verify.py` and its two `.drup` files. It then replays their `G.P111.zero-exclusion`, `G.P104-44.zero-exclusion`, `G.line-orbits` and `G.frame-orbits`, and matches the pivots by root vectors. All pass locally on Python 3.14.
- `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

## Not checked or not covered

- **The 896 admissible P104 units**, which have two-row classes. This is the open next question. PR #1292 gives only local rigidity there.
- **Nine or more costly terms.**
- **Zero exclusion** is #1212's DRUP result, replayed but not re-derived. PR968's F6 premise is inherited.
- There has been no independent human review of the written proof.
- All inherited conditions of the selected record remain.

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`), refined to the #1212 §10 obligations on P111 and type (4,4). Chooser nonce `118c1c4d3856655a6b7cb222d8d50aef`, track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2.
- **Heads:** base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; depends on #1212 head `57099cb5684f38877f31d149d598801671a633db`.
- **Claim:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1384. This is the next step named in #1212's handoff in #1166.
- **Overlap:** no other claim or PR on P111 or type-(4,4) global rigidity. The overlap search was refreshed before submission. #1292 and #1367 address local (tangent) rigidity on P104.

- **Navinor (#1292):** local P104 rigidity.
